verdict: EMCOR posted record revenue of $5.5B, up 29%, and record profit as its electrical and mechanical construction businesses surged — and its backlog of contracted work jumped 47% to $18.6B.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Record revenue of $5.54B, vs $4.30B a year ago; organic growth was 25.5%

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs $6.57 a year ago; non-GAAP diluted EPS was $9.60, excluding an impairment

kpis.label: Remaining performance obligations
kpis.note: Contracted work still to be done — a record, up 47.2% from a year ago

kpis.label: Operating margin
kpis.note: 10.5% on the company's non-GAAP basis, excluding the impairment

segments.name: US mechanical construction & facilities services
segments.note: Building and servicing heating, cooling, plumbing and piping systems — the largest business, and the joint-fastest growing. Revenue is reported in thousands; this is $2,546,679 thousand.

segments.name: US electrical construction & facilities services
segments.note: Wiring and electrical systems for buildings and infrastructure, plus related services — up 44% on strong project demand.

segments.name: US building services
segments.note: Ongoing facilities services — maintenance, operations and energy services for buildings.

segments.name: US industrial services
segments.note: Services for industrial plants such as refineries and factories — essentially flat at $288M.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling and running the company — 9.5% of revenue, down from 10.0% a year ago as revenue grew faster than overhead.

opex.name: Impairment loss on identifiable intangible assets
opex.note: A non-cash write-down of intangible assets from a past acquisition — the quarter's one-off item (see below).

follow100Note: Rows may add to $100.01 rather than $100.00 due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Record quarter, led by construction
takeaways.text: Revenue hit a record $5.54B, up 28.8% — 25.5% of that was organic growth, with acquisitions and the 2025 sale of the UK business making up the rest. US mechanical revenue rose 43% to $2.55B and US electrical 44% to $1.85B. The company raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $20.6B–$21.0B.

takeaways.title: The order book is the story
takeaways.text: Remaining performance obligations — work under contract but not yet done — reached a record $18.57B, up 47.2% from $12.61B a year ago, on new awards across most of the sectors EMCOR serves. That is more than three quarters of revenue already booked.

takeaways.title: One impairment hides a cleaner number
takeaways.text: GAAP diluted EPS was $9.04, up 37.6%. Excluding a $34M non-cash impairment of intangible assets ($24.7M after tax), non-GAAP EPS was $9.60 and non-GAAP operating income $579.8M at a 10.5% margin. The company also added $500M to its share buyback program.

oneTimers: A $34.0M non-cash impairment loss on identifiable intangible assets ($24.7M after tax) is included in operating income. Excluding it, non-GAAP operating income was $579.8M and non-GAAP net income was $424.7M, or $9.60 per diluted share.
otherDetail: Other income of $4M is interest income, net ($3.8M as reported).
footerNote: EMCOR reports in thousands; figures are rounded to $M (revenue $5,541.5M, net income $399.9M), with $1M of rounding absorbed in cost of sales (exact $4,433.3M) so the rounded lines balance. The UK building services business was sold in 2025 and contributed no revenue this quarter.
